title: Where the returners stand (Berakhot 34b)
hook: where those who have returned stand, even the perfectly righteous cannot
tomorrow: is eating an apple without a word a kind of taking?

segments.voice: Yesterday, when it flows: Chanina felt his prayer run free in his mouth, and said he was no prophet. Today, the same page, and a place to stand.

Screenshots last forever. Someone changes, really changes, and the group chat still has the receipts from who they used to be. Every time they do something good, somebody scrolls up. So who stands where even the perfectly good can't? The Talmud's answer is a surprise. Rabbi Abbahu says: in the place where those who return stand, even the completely righteous cannot stand. The person with the receipts gets the higher ground.
screen: `THE GROUP CHAT HAS RECEIPTS.` → `WHO STANDS HIGHER?` → `THE ONES WHO RETURNED.`

segments.voice: The returners have a name in Hebrew: baalei teshuvah, people of return. Teshuvah means turning back, to God and to who you were meant to be. Rabbi Abbahu finds his proof in a line from Isaiah: peace, peace, to the one who is far and to the one who is near. Far comes first. The one who was far away and came back is greeted before the one who never left. Then the Talmud does what it does: someone disagrees. Rabbi Yochanan reads it differently, and says the prophets' promises were spoken for the returners, while what waits for the completely righteous is something no eye has seen. So the sages argue about the ranking, and neither of them looks down on the person who came back. That matters this week, not in heaven. Elsewhere the Mishnah makes it law: you may not say to someone who has returned, remember what you used to do. Scrolling up is the very thing it rules out. Here's a way to hear Rabbi Abbahu: the one who never fell hasn't had to climb. The returner knows exactly what pulls, and turned anyway, maybe more than once.
screen: `BAALEI TESHUVAH: PEOPLE OF RETURN.` · `PEACE TO THE FAR, THEN THE NEAR.` · `RABBI YOCHANAN DISAGREES.` · `DON'T SAY: REMEMBER WHAT YOU DID.` · then, large: `RETURNERS STAND HIGHER.`

segments.voice: Think of one person who has truly changed: a friend, a parent, maybe you. With a pen, write one sentence about who they are now, with nothing about who they used to be. Read it back slowly, and let it be the whole story for these two minutes.
screen: `SOMEONE WHO CHANGED.` · `ONE SENTENCE: WHO THEY ARE NOW.` · `NOTHING ABOUT BEFORE.`

segments.voice: Where the returners stand: Rabbi Abbahu's place, higher than the completely righteous, because the far one is greeted first.
A line to keep: returners stand higher, and nobody gets to scroll up on them. Thirty of fifty.

howItsDone: Jews call someone who has come back to God and to Jewish life a baal teshuvah, and Jewish law, from the Mishnah on, forbids reminding a returner of their past.

sources.ref: Babylonian Talmud, Berakhot 34b (Rabbi Abbahu: where returners stand, the completely righteous cannot; Rabbi Yochanan's differing view)
Isaiah 57:19 (peace, peace, to him that is far off and to him that is near)
Isaiah 64:3 (no eye has seen; cited by Rabbi Yochanan for the completely righteous)
Mishnah Bava Metzia 4:10 (one may not say to a penitent, remember your former deeds)
